mainTopic: The ברכות before קריאת שמע, ברכת התורה, and the one ברכה the כהנים said in the בית המקדש
overview: The גמרא first asks why the morning ברכה says 'יוצר אור ובורא חשך' instead of the nicer word 'נוגה'. 'We follow the פסוק' is rejected, because we do change 'רע' to 'הכל'. רבא answers that the day ברכה must mention night and the night ברכה must mention day, and אביי finds the 'day' in the evening words 'גולל אור מפני חשך'. The second morning ברכה is 'אהבה רבה' according to שמואל, while the רבנן say 'אהבת עולם'. Since 'אהבה רבה' also covers ברכת התורה, the גמרא lists four opinions on which kinds of learning need ברכת התורה, ending with רבא: even תלמוד. It then gives several wordings for ברכת התורה and concludes that we say all of them. Finally it quotes the משנה in תמיד, where the כהנים said 'one ברכה' before שמע, and asks which one it was. שמואל says אהבה רבה. The answer יוצר אור, reported in the name of ריש לקיש, turns out to be an inference from his rule that the ברכות do not hold each other back. That inference continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The opening words of the morning blessing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the opening of the first morning blessing before קריאת שמע: 'יוצר אור ובורא חשך'.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Who forms light and creates darkness.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the text of the ברכה it is about to discuss. This line sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These words come almost exactly from ישעיה מ״ה:ז. The ברכה praises ה׳ as the Creator of both light and darkness. Everything that follows next asks why we keep the word חשך.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Who forms light', the name and opening of the first morning ברכה before קריאת שמע
Creates
Darkness

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the actual wording said every morning in שחרית, so the discussion explains our daily נוסח.

phrases.english: "Who forms light and creates darkness."
phrases.notes: Based on ישעיה מ״ה:ז.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the discussion of the wording of the ברכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The morning blessing opens with 'יוצר אור ובורא חשך'.

steps.title: Why not say brightness instead of darkness
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests replacing 'חשך' with 'נוגה' (brightness) so that the ברכה does not mention something negative.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him say: 'Who forms light and creates brightness'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why we mention darkness in a blessing at all. It offers a nicer word, 'נוגה', in its place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Darkness sounds negative, and a ברכה should use pleasant language. The word 'לימא' with an exclamation shows that the גמרא is pushing back on the wording, not just asking for information.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him say, a suggestion that challenges the current wording
Brightness, glow

phrases.english: Let him say: "Who forms light and creates brightness"!
phrases.notes: Proposes a more positive word than 'darkness'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording quoted in step 1.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברכה should use pleasant language, so we should say 'נוגה' instead of the negative word 'חשך'.

steps.title: We say it the way the verse is written
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that we keep 'חשך' because we follow the exact wording of the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: We say it as it is written.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the word 'חשך'. Its answer is that the ברכה copies the wording of the פסוק in ישעיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason is not that darkness is a good word. The reason is that we do not change a פסוק's wording when we use it as a ברכה. Respect for the text of the פסוק outweighs the wish for nicer language.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is written in the פסוק
We say

phrases.english: We say it as it is written.
phrases.notes: We follow the verse's wording exactly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Appeal to the wording of the source פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We could swap in a nicer word like 'נוגה'.
steps.terutzMaskana: We keep 'חשך' because the ברכה follows the פסוק word for word.

steps.title: But we do change 'evil' to 'all things'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the answer. The same פסוק says 'ובורא רע', yet we say 'הכל' to use a nicer word. So we should also say 'נוגה' instead of 'חשך'.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, take 'Who makes peace and creates evil.' Do we say that as it is written?! Rather, the verse says 'evil' and we read 'all things' to use nicer language. Here too, let us say 'brightness' to use nicer language!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the answer of step 3 by pointing to the second half of the same פסוק. There, we do change the wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule 'we follow the פסוק exactly' is not true, because we change 'רע' to 'הכל' as a לישנא מעליא. If we change one word of this פסוק for nicer language, we should change 'חשך' to 'נוגה' for the same reason. The next step answers this challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so, introduces a challenge built on the answer just given
Who makes peace and creates evil, the second half of the פסוק
All things, the word we say in place of 'רע'
Refined language, a polite substitute for an unpleasant word
Here too

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the ברכה really says 'ובורא רע'. The פסוק says 'רע', but our ברכה says 'ובורא את הכל'. That change is the whole basis of this challenge.
steps.whatToRemember: We already change 'רע' to 'הכל' for nicer language, so 'we follow the פסוק exactly' cannot explain why we keep 'חשך'. The גמרא will need a different reason, and that reason comes next.

phrases.english: But if so, "Who makes peace and creates evil":
phrases.notes: The continuation of the same verse.

phrases.english: do we say that as it is written?!
phrases.notes: Rhetorical: clearly we do not.

phrases.english: Rather, it is written "evil" and we read "all things"
phrases.notes: Our ברכה says 'ובורא את הכל'.

phrases.english: as a refined expression;
phrases.notes: A polite substitute for an unpleasant word.

phrases.english: here too, let us say "brightness"
phrases.notes: Apply the same logic to 'darkness'.

phrases.english: as a refined expression!
phrases.notes: The next step answers this challenge.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 3 and brings back the challenge of step 2.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: We already change 'רע' to 'הכל' in this very פסוק for nicer language. So following the פסוק exactly is not our rule, and 'חשך' should likewise become 'נוגה'.

steps.title: רבא's new reason: mention day at night and night by day
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that we keep 'חשך' in order to mention the quality of night during the day, just as we mention the quality of day at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: we say 'חשך' in order to mention the quality of day at night and the quality of night during the day.
steps.whatsHappening: The earlier answer ('we follow the פסוק') failed, so רבא gives a brand-new reason for keeping the word 'חשך'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אלא' tells us the old answer is dropped. The new reason is not about copying the פסוק. It is about the content: the day ברכה should mention night, and the night ברכה should mention day. That is why 'חשך' stays, while 'רע' can still be changed to 'הכל'.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. Signals that the previous answer is dropped and a new one is coming.
The quality or attribute of day (light)
The quality or attribute of night (darkness)
To mention

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying we copy the פסוק. That answer was already rejected. His reason is that night itself must be mentioned during the day, so 'נוגה' (brightness) would not do the job.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why 'חשך' stays but 'רע' becomes 'הכל'. Mentioning darkness has its own purpose. Mentioning evil does not.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
phrases.notes: 'אלא' replaces the rejected answer from Step 3

phrases.english: in order to mention the attribute of day at night
and the attribute of night during the day.
phrases.notes: In the morning we mention 'חשך' (night)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer from Step 3, which Step 4 knocked down, with a new reason for keeping 'חשך'.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We would think 'חשך' should become 'נוגה', since we soften 'רע' to 'הכל'.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'חשך' stays because the day ברכה must mention night, which 'נוגה' would not do.

steps.title: Where does the night blessing mention day?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees that the morning ברכה mentions night, but asks where the evening ברכה mentions day.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that night is mentioned during the day, as we say 'Who forms light and creates darkness'. But where do you find day mentioned at night?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא: his rule needs both halves, but only one half seems to exist.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'בשלמא' means 'I accept this part.' The morning ברכה clearly mentions darkness. The problem is the other direction: רבא said day is also mentioned at night, but the evening ברכה seems to have no 'יוצר אור'.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / it makes sense (accepts one part before challenging another)
As we say
Where do you find it? (how is it possible?)

phrases.english: Granted, the attribute of night during the day
as we say: 'Who forms light and creates darkness',
phrases.notes: The morning ברכה

phrases.english: but the attribute of day at night,
where do you find it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second half of רבא's rule from Step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that day is mentioned at night
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The evening ברכה seems to have no mention of light, so the 'day at night' half of the rule seems to have no source.

steps.title: אביי: 'Rolling away light before darkness'
steps.stepSummary: אביי shows that the evening ברכה does mention day: 'גולל אור מפני חשך וחשך מפני אור'.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The words 'He rolls away light before darkness and darkness before light' (in the evening ברכה) mention day at night.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge by pointing to a phrase in the evening ברכה that mentions light.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The evening ברכה (מעריב ערבים) says that ה׳ rolls away light before darkness and darkness before light. That phrase mentions light, so day really is mentioned at night. רבא's rule holds in both directions.

keyTerms.meaning: Rolls away
Before / in the face of

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's reason: the morning ברכה mentions darkness ('ובורא חשך') and the evening ברכה mentions light ('גולל אור מפני חשך'). Each time of day mentions the other.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
'Rolling away light before darkness
phrases.notes: From the evening ברכה 'המעריב ערבים'

phrases.english: and darkness before light.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 6 and saves רבא's rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to an existing text (the evening ברכה) that fits the rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The evening ברכה seemed to have no mention of day.
steps.terutzMaskana: The words 'גולל אור מפני חשך' mention day at night, so רבא's rule works in both directions.

steps.title: What is the other blessing before קריאת שמע?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the wording of the second morning ברכה before קריאת שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the other ברכה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new question: after 'יוצר אור', how does the second ברכה before שמע open? This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says two ברכות are said before שמע in the morning. The first, 'יוצר אור', has now been discussed. This short question opens the topic of the second ברכה.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one
What is it?

phrases.english: And what is the other one?
phrases.notes: The second ברכה before שמע in the morning

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the first ברכה and opens a new topic: the second ברכה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The opening words of the second morning ברכה before קריאת שמע

steps.title: The second blessing is 'אהבה רבה'
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה, quoting שמואל, says the second ברכה is 'אהבה רבה'. רבי אלעזר taught the same to his son רבי פדת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: 'אהבה רבה' (an abounding love). And רבי אלעזר also instructed his son, רבי פדת, to say 'אהבה רבה'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: the second ברכה opens with 'אהבה רבה'. A second authority who taught the same thing backs this up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's ruling gives the opening words. The extra report about רבי אלעזר teaching his son shows that this wording was a living, practical instruction, not just theory.

keyTerms.meaning: An abounding love (opening words of the second ברכה)
And likewise
Instructed him / ruled for him
His son

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
'An abounding love.'
And likewise Rabbi Elazar instructed
phrases.notes: Supporting tradition

phrases.english: Rabbi Pedat, his son,
'An abounding love.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The second ברכה opens with 'אהבה רבה', according to שמואל, and רבי אלעזר instructed his son the same way.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the wording 'אהבה רבה'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא backs up שמואל's ruling: the second ברכה is 'אהבה רבה', not 'אהבת עולם'.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא: we do not say 'אהבת עולם' (eternal love). We say 'אהבה רבה' (abounding love).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that agrees with what רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל in the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 9, שמואל said the second ברכה is 'אהבה רבה'. Now an older source, a ברייתא, says the same thing and even rejects the other wording, 'אהבת עולם'. So שמואל's ruling now has earlier support.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (in a ברייתא). A formula that brings support.
A teaching from the time of the תנאים that was not included in the משנה
'Eternal love', the other possible opening of the ברכה
We do not say

phrases.english: It was also taught so (in a baraita):
phrases.notes: Standard formula for bringing support to an earlier statement.

phrases.english: One does not say 'eternal love',
rather, 'abounding love'.
phrases.notes: This matches שמואל's ruling exactly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer given in step 9 with an earlier source.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's ruling that the second morning ברכה is 'אהבה רבה'
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא stating: אין אומרים אהבת עולם אלא אהבה רבה

steps.title: The רבנן say 'אהבת עולם', based on a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: Inside the same ברייתא, the רבנן disagree. They hold the wording should be 'אהבת עולם' and bring a פסוק from ירמיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the רבנן say we should say 'אהבת עולם'. And so the פסוק says: 'And an eternal love I have loved you, therefore I have drawn you with kindness' (ירמיהו 31:3).
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and records a second opinion. The רבנן say the ברכה should open with 'אהבת עולם'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So the ברייתא contains a disagreement. The first opinion says 'אהבה רבה'. The רבנן say 'אהבת עולם', because that exact phrase appears in a פסוק about ה׳'s love for כלל ישראל. Each side has its own reason for its wording.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, often the majority opinion
And so the פסוק says. Introduces a supporting verse.
I have drawn you (close)
Kindness

steps.whyThisMatters: The two opinions are reflected in practice today. נוסח אשכנז says 'אהבה רבה' at שחרית and 'אהבת עולם' at מעריב. נוסח ספרד and the עדות המזרח say 'אהבת עולם' in the morning as well.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say: 'eternal love',
and so it (the verse) says:
'And an eternal love I have loved you,
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 31:3

phrases.english: therefore I have drawn you with kindness.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents the opposing opinion within the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the רבנן, the ברכה opens with 'אהבת עולם', following the language of the פסוק in ירמיהו.

steps.title: 'אהבה רבה' also counts as the ברכה on learning Torah
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that someone who gets up early to learn needs a ברכת התורה before קריאת שמע. After קריאת שמע he does not need one, because 'אהבה רבה' already covered it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: If someone woke up early to learn, then until he has said קריאת שמע he must say a ברכה. Once he has said קריאת שמע he does not need to say a ברכה, because he already fulfilled his obligation with 'אהבה רבה'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling that uses the ברכה of 'אהבה רבה' for something else: it can also serve as the ברכה on learning Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אהבה רבה' asks ה׳ to help us learn and understand His Torah, so it contains the same ideas as ברכת התורה. That is why once you have said it, you have 'been exempted' from a separate ברכת התורה. The question is only about timing: before saying it you still need a ברכה, and after saying it you do not.

keyTerms.meaning: He woke up early
To learn or review Torah
He became exempt, his obligation was already covered
The ברכה said before learning Torah
He must say a ברכה

steps.confusionAlert: The 'ברכה' that is needed here is ברכת התורה, the ברכה on learning Torah. It is not the ברכות of קריאת שמע themselves.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
If one woke up early to learn,

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁלֹּא קָרָא קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע — צָרִיךְ לְבָרֵךְ.
phrases.english: as long as he has not yet recited Shema, he must recite a blessing.
phrases.notes: Meaning ברכת התורה.

phrases.aramaic: מִשֶּׁקָּרָא קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע — אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ לְבָרֵךְ,
phrases.english: Once he has recited Shema, he need not recite a blessing,
since he was already exempted by 'abounding love'.
phrases.notes: 'אהבה רבה' contains praise and requests about the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הִשְׁכִּים לִשְׁנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the mention of 'אהבה רבה' and opens a new topic: ברכת התורה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Before קריאת שמע, someone learning needs ברכת התורה. After קריאת שמע he does not, because 'אהבה רבה' already exempted him.

steps.title: רב הונא: מקרא needs a ברכה, מדרש does not
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that learning מקרא requires ברכת התורה, while learning מדרש does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: For learning מקרא (the written Torah), one must say a ברכה. For learning מדרש (deriving הלכות from the פסוקים), one does not need to say a ברכה.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that ברכת התורה has come up, the גמרא asks a new question: which kinds of Torah learning need this ברכה? רב הונא gives the first opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא draws the line at the written words of ה׳. The פסוקים themselves (מקרא) need a ברכה. Learning that explains and derives laws from them (מדרש) does not.

keyTerms.meaning: The written Torah, the text of the פסוקים
Here: halachic derivation of laws from the פסוקים
An אמורא, student of רב

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'מדרש' means halachic derivation of laws from the פסוקים. It does not mean the stories of מדרש אגדה.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
For (learning) Scripture one must recite a blessing,
and for midrash (halakhic derivation), one need not recite a blessing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: לַמִּקְרָא צָרִיךְ לְבָרֵךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from when ברכת התורה is said to what kind of learning needs it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only מקרא requires ברכת התורה. מדרש does not.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: מקרא and מדרש need a ברכה, משנה does not
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר disagrees with רב הונא. Both מקרא and מדרש need ברכת התורה, and only משנה does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: For מקרא and for מדרש one must say a ברכה. For משנה one does not need to say a ברכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second opinion that disagrees with רב הונא and widens which kinds of learning need a ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר includes מדרש, because מדרש is tied directly to the פסוקים it explains. משנה is a list of rulings without the פסוקים behind them, so according to him it does not need a ברכה. The argument is about how close a type of learning must be to the written Torah to need its own ברכה.

keyTerms.meaning: The rulings of the תנאים, stated without their source פסוקים
An אמורא in ארץ ישראל
He does not need to say a ברכה

steps.whatToRemember: There is a spectrum of opinions about which learning needs ברכת התורה. רב הונא: only מקרא. רבי אלעזר: מקרא and מדרש, but not משנה. The גמרא will continue with opinions that include even more.
steps.whyThisMatters: The opinions narrow the gap between the written Torah and the oral Torah step by step. This sets up רבא's widest opinion in step 16 and the proof from רב's practice in step 17.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:
For Scripture and for midrash one must recite a blessing,
for Mishnah one need not recite a blessing.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר: לַמִּקְרָא וְלַמִּדְרָשׁ צָרִיךְ לְבָרֵךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב הונא by adding מדרש to the category that requires a ברכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מקרא and מדרש require ברכת התורה. משנה does not.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: משנה also needs a blessing, but תלמוד does not
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן widens the rule: מקרא, מדרש and also משנה need ברכת התורה. Only תלמוד does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: Even for משנה you must also say a ברכה. But for תלמוד you do not need to say a ברכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third opinion in the growing list. רבי יוחנן adds משנה to the things that need ברכת התורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא said only מקרא needs a ברכה. רבי אלעזר added מדרש. Now רבי יוחנן adds משנה too, and leaves out only תלמוד, which is the discussion and reasoning behind the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Even (signals going further than the last opinion)
Also, too
Analysis of the משנה, explaining its reasons
One must say a ברכה

steps.confusionAlert: Here תלמוד does not mean 'the Talmud book.' It means the activity of explaining and analyzing the reasons behind the משנה.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
Even for Mishnah, one must also recite a blessing,
but for Talmud, one need not recite a blessing.
phrases.notes: The square brackets mark words the editors added as a correction (based on other readings). They are not in the standard printed text.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אַף לַמִּשְׁנָה נָמֵי צָרִיךְ לְבָרֵךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes one level further than רבי אלעזר in Step 14 by adding משנה to the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מקרא, מדרש and משנה all need ברכת התורה. תלמוד does not.

steps.title: רבא: even תלמוד needs a blessing
steps.stepSummary: רבא holds that every kind of learning needs ברכת התורה, even תלמוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: Even for תלמוד you must say a ברכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the last and widest opinion. רבא says even תלמוד needs ברכת התורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each opinion went one step further, and רבא finishes the list: no kind of Torah learning is left out. The reasoning is that תלמוד, which explains the reasons of the law, is also full Torah learning.

keyTerms.meaning: A later אמורא; gives the widest opinion here
To go back and bless again (a variant reading)

steps.whatToRemember: Four levels: רב הונא (only מקרא), רבי אלעזר (מקרא and מדרש), רבי יוחנן (also משנה), רבא (also תלמוד, meaning everything).

phrases.english: And Rava said:
Even for Talmud, one must recite a blessing.
phrases.notes: The words in round brackets ('to go back and bless') appear in the standard printed text, and the editors mark them for removal. The square-bracket word ('to bless') is the corrected reading.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרָבָא אָמַר: אַף לַתַּלְמוּד צָרִיךְ לְבָרֵךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי יוחנן's exception for תלמוד and removes it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All Torah learning, including תלמוד, needs ברכת התורה.

steps.title: רב's practice before teaching the ספרא supports רבא
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בר אשי reports that רב would wash his hands and say a ברכה before teaching the ספרא. This supports רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רב חייא בר אשי said: Many times I stood before רב to review our chapter in the ספרא of רב's school. רב would first wash his hands, say a ברכה, and then teach us our chapter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story as a proof for רבא. רב always said a ברכה before teaching, even when the learning was the deep, reason-based kind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ספרא is a מדרש on ויקרא, but רב taught it with explanations and reasons, which is really תלמוד-style learning. Since רב still said a ברכה first, this shows that even תלמוד needs a ברכה, just as רבא said.

keyTerms.meaning: Many times
Before רב
To review or learn our chapter
The ספרא (תורת כהנים) of רב's study hall, a מדרש on ויקרא
Does first, ahead of time
Washes his hands

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a proof from what a great רב actually did, not only from his words. That kind of proof gives רבא's opinion real practical weight.

phrases.english: For Rav Chiyya bar Ashi said:
Many times I would stand
before Rav to review our chapter
in the 'Sifra of the school of Rav,'
phrases.notes: Also called תורת כהנים, the halachic מדרש on ויקרא.

phrases.english: he would first wash his hands,
and recite a blessing, and teach us our chapter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up רבא's opinion from Step 16.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's ruling that even תלמוד needs ברכת התורה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's practice, reported by his student רב חייא בר אשי, of saying a ברכה before teaching the ספרא with explanations.

steps.title: What blessing does one say?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the actual words of ברכת התורה are.
steps.simpleTranslation: What ברכה does he say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. Now that we know when to bless, it asks what the words of the ברכה are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the topic was which learning needs a ברכה. This question changes the topic to the wording itself, and the answer comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: What does he bless? (asking for the wording)

phrases.english: What blessing does he recite?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the question of when to bless to the question of what to say.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact wording of ברכת התורה.

steps.title: שמואל's wording: commanded us to engage in words of Torah
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes שמואל: the ברכה is 'אשר קדשנו במצותיו וצונו לעסוק בדברי תורה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: 'Who made us holy with His מצוות and commanded us to busy ourselves with the words of Torah.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with שמואל's wording. It uses the normal form of a ברכה said on a מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This wording treats learning Torah like any other מצוה, using 'אשר קדשנו במצותיו וצונו'. The word 'לעסוק' (to be busy with) shows the מצוה is to be involved in learning, not only to finish it.

keyTerms.meaning: Who made us holy with His מצוות
And commanded us
To engage in, to be busy with
Words or matters of Torah

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the first of the ברכות התורה we say every morning. The גמרא will go on to bring more wordings.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
'Who sanctified us with His commandments
and commanded us to engage in matters of Torah.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in Step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברכה is 'אשר קדשנו במצותיו וצונו לעסוק בדברי תורה'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ברכת התורה uses the standard ברכה form for a מצוה, with 'לעסוק בדברי תורה'.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's ending: make the Torah sweet
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן finishes the ברכה with a prayer that the Torah be sweet in our mouths. It closes with 'המלמד תורה לעמו ישראל'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן ends the ברכה like this: 'Please make the words of Your Torah sweet, ה׳ our God, in our mouths and in the mouths of Your people, the house of Israel. May we, our children, and the children of Your people, the house of Israel, all know Your Name and learn Your Torah. Blessed are You, ה׳, Who teaches Torah to His people Israel.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי יוחנן's addition to the ברכה that שמואל just taught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל gave the opening words, 'לעסוק בדברי תורה'. רבי יוחנן attaches a closing request to that same ברכה. He asks that learning feel sweet, and that our children also become people who learn Torah. His ending is a full ברכה ending, 'ברוך אתה ה' המלמד תורה לעמו ישראל'.

keyTerms.meaning: ends it with, adds a closing to it
please make sweet
our children and descendants
Who teaches Torah to His people Israel

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן is not giving a brand-new, separate ברכה here. The words 'מסיים בה' tell you he is adding an ending to שמואל's ברכה.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan concludes it like this:
phrases.notes: 'It' means שמואל's ברכה from the previous step.

phrases.english: "Please make sweet, ה׳ our God,
the words of Your Torah in our mouths
and in the mouths of Your people, the house of Israel,
and may we and our descendants
and the descendants of Your people, the house of Israel,
all of us be knowers of Your Name and learners of Your Torah.
Blessed are You, ה׳,
Who teaches Torah to His people Israel."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a closing section to שמואל's ברכה from Step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ברכת התורה continues with 'הערב נא' and ends with 'המלמד תורה לעמו ישראל'.

steps.title: רב המנונא's version: Who chose us and gave us the Torah
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא gives another wording for ברכת התורה, 'אשר בחר בנו', which ends with 'נותן התורה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב המנונא said: 'Who chose us from all the nations and gave us His Torah. Blessed are You, ה׳, Giver of the Torah.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third wording for ברכת התורה, this one from רב המנונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's ברכה focuses on the מצוה of learning. רבי יוחנן's ending focuses on learning feeling sweet and passing it to our children. רב המנונא's ברכה focuses on a different point: thanking ה׳ for choosing us and giving us the Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: Who chose us
Giver of the Torah

phrases.english: And Rav Hamnuna said:
"Who chose us from all the nations
and gave us His Torah.
Blessed are You, ה׳, Giver of the Torah."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another answer to the question in Step 18 about the words of the ברכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ברכת התורה is 'אשר בחר בנו מכל העמים ונתן לנו את תורתו, ברוך אתה ה' נותן התורה'.

steps.title: רב המנונא praises this ברכה as the best
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא says his ברכה is the finest of all the ברכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא said: This is the best of the ברכות.
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא praises the ברכה he just gave. He calls it the most excellent of the ברכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This step does not add new words to say. It ranks רב המנונא's ברכה above the others. The likely reason is that it thanks ה׳ for choosing כלל ישראל and for giving the Torah itself.

keyTerms.meaning: the best of the blessings

phrases.english: Rav Hamnuna said:
This is the most excellent of the blessings.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הַמְנוּנָא: זוֹ הִיא מְעוּלָּה שֶׁבַּבְּרָכוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב המנונא comments on and praises his own ברכה from Step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'אשר בחר בנו' is the most outstanding of the Torah ברכות.

steps.title: Therefore we say all of them
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that we should say all the versions of ברכת התורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore, let us say all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the question of which wording to use. Instead of choosing one, we say all of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each version has its own strength. That is why the גמרא does not pick one: it combines them. This is the source for our daily practice of saying 'לעסוק בדברי תורה', then 'והערב נא', then 'אשר בחר בנו'.

keyTerms.meaning: therefore
let us say all of them

steps.whatToRemember: Every morning we say three parts of ברכת התורה: 'לעסוק בדברי תורה' with 'והערב נא' (שמואל and רבי יוחנן), and 'אשר בחר בנו' (רב המנונא). This is because the גמרא said 'לימרינהו לכולהו'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This line is the direct source of the ברכות התורה printed in every סידור.

phrases.english: Therefore, let us say all of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion of the ברכה's wording by combining all the versions.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: All the versions of ברכת התורה are said together.

steps.title: The משנה in תמיד: the כהנים' ברכות in the בית המקדש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה in תמיד. The supervisor told the כהנים to say one ברכה. They then read the עשרת הדברות and קריאת שמע, and said three ברכות. On שבת they added a ברכה for the outgoing משמר.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there, in a משנה: The supervisor said to them, 'Say one ברכה!' And they said a ברכה. They read the עשרת הדברות, 'שמע', 'והיה אם שמוע', and 'ויאמר'. They blessed the people with three ברכות: 'אמת ויציב', 'עבודה', and ברכת כהנים. On שבת they added one ברכה for the משמר that was leaving.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new section by quoting a משנה about the morning service of the כהנים in the בית המקדש. This is setting up the next move: the גמרא will soon ask which 'one ברכה' the כהנים said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברכות of קריאת שמע are the main topic of this פרק. This משנה shows what the כהנים did in the בית המקדש. They said only one ברכה before שמע, and they added the עשרת הדברות. After שמע they said 'אמת ויציב' along with other ברכות. The unclear phrase 'ברכה אחת' is the hook for the coming discussion.

keyTerms.meaning: we learned there, in a משנה elsewhere (here, מסכת תמיד)
the appointed supervisor of the כהנים
the Ten Commandments
the ברכה of גאולה said after שמע
a ברכה asking ה׳ to accept the קרבנות
the group of כהנים finishing its week, which switched on שבת

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה does not tell us which 'ברכה אחת' the כהנים said. Do not assume it was one of the three listed later. Those three were said after שמע. The גמרא will ask about this right away.
steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה becomes the base text for the discussion about which ברכה comes before קריאת שמע, and why the עשרת הדברות are not read today.

phrases.english: We learned there (in a mishna):
phrases.notes: The משנה is in מסכת תמיד.

phrases.english: The appointed supervisor said to them:
"Recite one blessing!"
And they recited a blessing.
And they read the Ten Commandments,
Shema, VeHaya im Shamoa, and VaYomer.
And they blessed the people with three blessings:
True and Firm, Avoda, and the priestly blessing.
And on Shabbat they add one blessing
for the outgoing priestly watch.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves ברכת התורה and returns to the פרק's main topic, the ברכות of קריאת שמע, by quoting a new source.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the בית המקדש the כהנים said one ברכה, then the עשרת הדברות and the three parts of שמע, then 'אמת ויציב', 'עבודה', and ברכת כהנים. On שבת they added a ברכה for the outgoing משמר.

steps.title: What was the one ברכה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the 'one ברכה' in the משנה in תמיד was.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the 'one ברכה' that the משנה mentions?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה it just quoted and asks which ברכה the כהנים said first. This question sets up the answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only says 'they said one ברכה' and does not name it. Before קריאת שמע there are two ברכות, יוצר אור and אהבה רבה. So it is not clear which one the משנה means.

keyTerms.meaning: What is?
One blessing

phrases.english: What is 'one blessing'?
phrases.notes: This refers to the משנה in תמיד quoted in Step 24.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of an unclear phrase in the משנה quoted in Step 24.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which of the ברכות before קריאת שמע was the 'one ברכה' the כהנים said.

steps.title: The story of the question, and שמואל's answer: אהבה רבה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא and רבי יוסי בר אבא were asked this question and did not know the answer. Neither did רב מתנה. רב יהודה finally answered in the name of שמואל: אהבה רבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like the time רבי אבא and רבי יוסי בר אבא came to a certain place. The people there asked them, 'What is the one ברכה?' They did not know. They went and asked רב מתנה, and he did not know either. They went and asked רב יהודה. He told them: 'This is what שמואל said: אהבה רבה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a story. Several great חכמים could not answer it until רב יהודה quoted שמואל: the one ברכה was אהבה רבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story shows that this question was not simple, because even big תלמידי חכמים did not have the answer ready. שמואל's answer is the second ברכה before קריאת שמע, the one about ה׳'s love and the gift of the Torah. That fits well with the כהנים then reading the עשרת הדברות and קריאת שמע.

keyTerms.meaning: They happened to come to
A place
They did not have it in hand (they did not know the answer)
They asked him
'Great love', the second ברכה before קריאת שמע

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הָא דְּרַבִּי אַבָּא וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר אַבָּא
phrases.english: Like that story of Rabbi Abba and Rabbi Yosei bar Abba
phrases.notes: The answer is given through a story.

phrases.english: who happened to come to a certain place,
they asked them: What is 'one blessing'?
They did not have the answer.
They came and asked Rav Masna,
and he did not have the answer.
They came and asked Rav Yehuda.
He said to them: This is what Shmuel said:
'Great love' (Ahava Rabba).

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָא דְּרַבִּי אַבָּא וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from Step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: According to שמואל, the one ברכה was אהבה רבה.

steps.title: ריש לקיש's answer: יוצר אור
steps.stepSummary: A chain of transmission reports that רבי שמעון בן לקיש said the one ברכה was יוצר אור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זריקא said in the name of רבי אמי, who said in the name of רבי שמעון בן לקיש: 'יוצר אור.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second answer. According to ריש לקיש, as רבי זריקא reported it, the one ברכה was יוצר אור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This disagrees with שמואל. יוצר אור is the first ברכה before קריאת שמע, which praises ה׳ for creating daylight. So there are now two different answers to the question.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Who forms light', the first ברכה before קריאת שמע
ריש לקיש, a great אמורא in ארץ ישראל

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי זְרִיקָא, אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי,
phrases.english: And Rabbi Zerika said that Rabbi Ami said
that Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
'Who forms light' (Yotzer Ohr).

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי זְרִיקָא, אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי, אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer from שמואל's answer in Step 26.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The one ברכה the כהנים said was יוצר אור.

steps.title: ריש לקיש did not say this outright
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בר יוסף says that the report in the name of ריש לקיש was not something he said directly. People worked it out from another statement of his.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב יצחק בר יוסף came from ארץ ישראל, he said: 'What רבי זריקא reported was not said explicitly. It was worked out from a general statement.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יצחק בר יוסף corrects how ריש לקיש's view was reported. ריש לקיש never actually said 'יוצר אור'. People concluded it from something else he said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This does not prove that the answer יוצר אור is wrong. It only says that it is an inference and not a direct quote. If the inference has a weak point, the answer could fall apart, so the גמרא will now check how the inference was made.

keyTerms.meaning: When he came (usually from ארץ ישראל to בבל)
It was said explicitly
It was said by inference (worked out from a general statement)

steps.confusionAlert: רב יצחק בר יוסף is not saying the answer יוצר אור is false. He is only saying that ריש לקיש never said those words. Others worked out his view from a different statement.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲתָא רַב יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף, אָמַר,
phrases.english: When Rav Yitzchak bar Yosef came, he said:

phrases.aramaic: הָא דְּרַבִּי זְרִיקָא לָאו בְּפֵירוּשׁ אִתְּמַר
phrases.english: That statement of Rabbi Zerika was not said explicitly,
rather, it was said by inference.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא דְּרַבִּי זְרִיקָא לָאו בְּפֵירוּשׁ אִתְּמַר אֶלָּא מִכְּלָלָא אִתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how the statement in Step 27 was passed down.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: It rejects only the claim that ריש לקיש said 'יוצר אור' explicitly. It does not reject the answer itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The report treated an inference as if it were a direct quote.

steps.title: ריש לקיש's actual statement: the ברכות do not hold each other back
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש actually said that the משנה in תמיד shows that the ברכות of קריאת שמע do not hold each other back.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי זריקא said in the name of רבי אמי, in the name of רבי שמעון בן לקיש: 'This shows that the ברכות do not hold each other back.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes what ריש לקיש really said. Because the כהנים said only 'one ברכה', we learn that each ברכה counts on its own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Do not hold each other back' means that if you say only one of the ברכות, you still fulfill your obligation for that one. ריש לקיש learned this from the fact that the כהנים said only one ברכה before קריאת שמע. He did not say which ברכה it was.

keyTerms.meaning: This shows (a conclusion drawn from a source)
They do not hold each other back (each one works on its own)

steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches a practical rule: if a person said only one of the ברכות of קריאת שמע, that ברכה still counts.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי זְרִיקָא אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי,
phrases.english: As Rabbi Zerika said that Rabbi Ami said
that Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
This shows

phrases.aramaic: בְּרָכוֹת אֵין מְעַכְּבוֹת זוֹ אֶת זוֹ.
phrases.english: that the blessings do not hold each other back.

steps.triggerLanguage: זֹאת אוֹמֶרֶת בְּרָכוֹת אֵין מְעַכְּבוֹת זוֹ אֶת זוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the original statement that Step 28 said the inference came from.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברכות of קריאת שמע do not hold each other back. Saying one of them is valid even without the other.

steps.title: How people concluded יוצר אור: it fits the rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to explain the inference. If the כהנים said יוצר אור and skipped אהבה רבה, that explains ריש לקיש's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well if you say they said יוצר אור. That is why the ברכות do not hold each other back: they did not say אהבה רבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to show why people thought ריש לקיש meant יוצר אור. This is only the first half of the argument, and the second half comes right on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the one ברכה was יוצר אור, the כהנים skipped אהבה רבה. Their ברכה still counted, which matches 'the ברכות do not hold each other back.' The 'בשלמא' wording tells us the גמרא will next show that the other option, אהבה רבה, does not fit as neatly.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well if you say (this sets up a contrast with the other option)
That is why / that explains
They used to say

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the end of the argument. The phrase 'אי אמרת בשלמא' always sets up a second half ('but if you say...'), and that comes in the next part of the גמרא.

phrases.aramaic: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא ״יוֹצֵר אוֹר״ הֲווֹ אָמְרִי,
phrases.english: It works well if you say they used to say 'Who forms light':

phrases.aramaic: הַיְינוּ דִּבְרָכוֹת אֵין מְעַכְּבוֹת זוֹ אֶת זוֹ,
phrases.english: that is why the blessings do not hold each other back,
since they did not say 'Great love'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא ״יוֹצֵר אוֹר״ הֲווֹ אָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the statement in Step 29 led to the answer יוצר אור reported in Step 27.
steps.raayaObject: That ריש לקיש held the one ברכה was יוצר אור.
steps.raayaSupportSource: His rule that the ברכות do not hold each other back, which fits if אהבה רבה was skipped.
